sections.html:
Ames is in Story County, central Iowa, about 30 miles north of Des Moines. The 2020 census counted 66,427 residents, making it the ninth-largest city in the state. A railroad-era street grid near downtown and newer growth farther out mean very different houses under one city name, so a buyer's expectations depend heavily on the neighborhood.

Iowa State University shapes the market more than anything else. Fall 2023 enrollment was 30,177 students, and the university employs 18,212 people, far ahead of any other local employer. Campustown, just south of campus, is a dense mix of student apartments, restaurants and nightlife. Because so much housing here is rented, the city's rental rules come up in many Ames sales.

Any rented property in Ames that is not owner-occupied must be registered with the city's Inspection Division. If you are selling a current or former rental, the registration status is part of the sale.

SituationWhat happens
Letter of ComplianceLasts one to four years and cannot be renewed without an inspection
Annual feeBased on property type, billed each May, due within 30 days; the billing period runs July 1 to June 30
Registered rental sellsRegistration transfers and no new inspection is required
Pre-sale inspection, property registeredFree
Pre-sale inspection, property not registered$56.10 fee

When a registered rental sells, you tell the Inspection Division who the buyer is, and the buyer registers the property in their own name. A buyer who wants a pre-sale inspection submits the registration form before purchase. Fees continue until the city receives a removal form, so if you stopped renting, ask the Inspection Division to confirm the form went through. Otherwise the fees keep accruing in your name.

Owner-occupied means a townhouse, condo or detached home lived in by the owner or a first-degree relative. One roomer, one exchange student, or a live-in nanny or nurse is allowed, but more than one of those makes the unit a rental. If a tenant is buying the home on contract, owner-occupied status requires a legally recorded contract with the Story County Recorder.

Some property types are exempt from registration altogether: owner-occupied single-family homes, bed and breakfasts that hold a license, hotels and motels, university housing, health and custodial facilities with a state license, and fraternity and sorority houses. Vacation lodging is not exempt just because it is short-term.

The city schedules an Ames rental inspection by email notice naming the date and the inspector. If you cannot attend, tell the city within five days.

The owner, a registered operator or an authorized representative must be present, and a tenant does not count as a representative. The owner or operator has to give tenants at least 24 hours' notice. There is no charge per inspection, and each structure gets one free appeal per inspection cycle. Extra appeals in the same cycle are charged at the standard rate.

Ames has warm summers and cold winters, with about 38 inches of precipitation and about 28 inches of snow in an average year. That shows up in roofs, gutters, basement drainage and furnace age. A buyer using a lender will often get an inspection report listing exactly those items, and repair requests can slow a conventional sale.

A cash buyer sees the same condition issues but does not need a lender's sign-off. That is the practical difference for a seller with an older furnace or a worn roof.

The Ames Community School District runs the public schools. CyRide is the city's bus system and the most-used transit system in Iowa, with over 4.7 million rides in 2024, so if you are selling a rental, tell the buyer which route serves the street. Ames Municipal Airport is about one mile southeast of the city.

If a house sits vacant while you decide, you still carry utilities, insurance and any annual rental registration fee until the city has the removal form. A quick sale caps those costs.

sections.h2: If you are selling a rental
sections.html:
A rental sale has more moving parts than a house you live in. Before you talk to any buyer, find out whether the property is registered, when the current Letter of Compliance ends and what the last annual fee was. The fee is billed each May and due within 30 days, so a sale in spring can overlap a bill. Ask the Inspection Division how it wants the buyer's name reported, because the registration moves to the buyer and the city has to know who that is.

Tenants matter next. Their lease end date decides when the buyer can take possession, and a tenant is not allowed to stand in for the owner at an inspection. If an inspection notice arrives while the house is under contract, tell the buyer and your closing agent right away, and remember you have five days to tell the city if you cannot attend.

Finally, keep your own records: the registration form, any compliance letter, inspection notices and proof that a removal form was filed if you ever stopped renting. These close out your responsibility cleanly and save a buyer from questions.

sections.h2: Deed paperwork for an Ames sale
sections.html:
Iowa recorders require a Declaration of Value with a deed, plus transfer tax on the sale price over $500 unless an exemption is stated on the document. The same items apply when the deed goes to the Story County Recorder.

The deed also needs a groundwater hazard statement, or a sentence on the first page saying the transaction is exempt. Since July 1, 2022, a seller can use the exemption if none of the listed conditions exist on the property. A recorder cannot record a deed without one or the other.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of an Ames house works
sections.html:
A cash sale follows a short sequence: you share the address and condition, we review it, and you receive a written offer you can accept or decline.

  • Send the address, the condition of the roof, furnace and plumbing, and whether the house is owner-occupied or rented.
  • Tell us if it is a registered rental so we can plan around the Inspection Division notice for the sale.
  • If tenants live there, tell us their lease end date.
  • A title company prepares the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement or its exemption sentence.
  • The deed is recorded with the Story County Recorder at closing.

If the house has a rental registration, a letter from the Inspection Division confirming its status can save time at closing. If you inherited the house and have not yet opened the estate, mention that too, because the court process comes before any sale.

faqs.q: How many people live in Ames?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 66,427 residents, which made Ames the ninth-largest city in Iowa.
Yes. Rented properties that are not owner-occupied must be registered with the city's Inspection Division, and a Letter of Compliance lasts one to four years depending on the inspection result.

faqs.q: What happens to an Ames rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: It transfers to the buyer without a new inspection. You notify the Inspection Division of the buyer's details, and the buyer registers the property in their own name.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Ames?
faqs.a: Iowa State University, with 18,212 employees in 2022. Mary Greeley Medical Center follows with 1,407.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ames house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not need to fix the roof, furnace or interior before closing. Disclose known problems accurately in the paperwork.
